stem: Which of the following is equal to ${=b}^{-\frac{{=m}}{{=n}}}$? Do not use a calculator.
solution: Write ${=b}$ as a power whose exponent is ${=n}$, the denominator of the exponent: ${=b}={=r}^{{=n}}$.
Multiply the exponents: ${=n}\times\left(-\frac{{=m}}{{=n}}\right)=-{=m}$, so the expression equals ${=r}^{-{=m}}$.
A negative exponent means the reciprocal: ${=r}^{-{=m}}=\frac{1}{{=r}^{{=m}}}=\frac{1}{{=rm}}$.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Drops the minus sign of the exponent
proposed_misconceptions.description: Evaluates the power as if the exponent were positive, so no reciprocal is taken: 64^(-2/3) is given as 16 instead of 1/16.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Reads a negative exponent as a negative answer
proposed_misconceptions.description: Treats the minus sign in the exponent as making the value negative: 64^(-2/3) is given as -16 instead of 1/16.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Ignores the numerator of the exponent
proposed_misconceptions.description: Takes only the root named by the denominator and the reciprocal, and forgets to raise to the numerator: 64^(-2/3) is given as 1/4 (the value of 64^(-1/3)) instead of 1/16.

notes: mcq because every wrong option is one specific, diagnosable error and the catalogue for this objective was empty (so the three ids are new, declared above). Exponent is -m/n in lowest terms with m of at least 2, so the numerator-ignored option (1/r) can never equal the correct 1/r^m; the three distractors (r^m, -r^m, 1/r) and the correct 1/r^m are always four different values (checked over all 15 instances). Bases are 4 up to 125 with answers 1/8 up to 1/243. Parent is the book's 27^(-1/3), which has m = 1; m of at least 2 is the small extension that makes the numerator error observable. Standard rather than advanced: one twist (the negative exponent) on a whole-number base.
